vfr.label: Variable frame rate
vfr.why: Frames are not evenly spaced in time. Editors expect a constant rate; uneven timing makes the timeline drift, audio slip out of sync, or the editor crash on import.

fps_mismatch.label: Frame rate
fps_mismatch.why: The clip runs at a different rate than your project. Mixing rates on one timeline forces the editor to drop or repeat frames on the fly, which looks choppy and costs playback speed.

hdr.label: HDR
hdr.why: HDR footage on a normal Rec.709 timeline looks washed out or clipped unless it is tone-mapped first.

hevc_10bit.label: 10-bit HEVC
hevc_10bit.why: 10-bit HEVC is very heavy to decode and not supported everywhere; scrubbing stutters or the clip refuses to play.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.why: Clips above the project size waste disk and processing power, and odd frame sizes make some codecs fail.

audio_rate.label: Audio rate
audio_rate.why: Video projects run at 48 kHz. Other rates get resampled during playback, which can drift over long clips.

rotation.label: Rotation in metadata
rotation.why: Phones store rotation as a flag. Some editors ignore it and show the clip sideways.

no_audio.label: No audio
no_audio.why: Without an audio track the clip behaves differently from the rest when you link or sync sound.

insv.label: Insta360 original
insv.why: 360° originals need reframing in Insta360 Studio before any editor can use them.

corrupt.label: Damaged file
corrupt.why: The file cannot be read reliably. Re-encoding would hide the damage, so Clipsana leaves it for you to check.

color_space.label: Colours
color_space.why: The pixels are coded in BT.601. On a Rec.709 timeline colours shift slightly unless they are converted.
